html:
The Battle of Carabobo was fought on 24 June 1821 on the plain of Carabobo, near Valencia in today's Venezuela. The army of Simón Bolívar beat the Spanish royalist army of Miguel de la Torre and won Venezuela's independence.

It was part of the Spanish American independence wars. Bolívar had freed neighbouring New Granada at Boyacá in 1819 and founded the republic of Gran Colombia. After a truce with Spain broke down, he gathered about 6,500 men to take Caracas. De la Torre, with about 5,000, blocked the road across the plain. Bolívar sent the plainsmen cavalry of José Antonio Páez and a legion of British volunteers along a hidden path through the hills to hit the royalist right side. The British held under heavy fire while the others formed up. Then the cavalry charged and the royalist army broke. The battle took about an hour. Only one royalist battalion got away in good order.

Bolívar entered Caracas five days later. The last royalists held out on the coast until 1823. With Venezuela safe, Bolívar turned south to free Ecuador and Peru, where the wars ended at Ayacucho. Venezuela marks 24 June as a national holiday.
